blocks.text: The Liberal government calls Bill C-39 one of the most important pieces of legislation in a generation. Critics say it threatens the fundamental rights of Canadians. It could become law by the end of the year.
Front Burner27:51Can Canada build fast without breaking things?

Bill C-39, the Building Canada Strong Act, is a behemoth: 243 pages containing 300-plus clauses that amend more than a dozen pieces of federal legislation. The Liberals call it one of the most important economic bills in a generation, a way to get major projects built faster.

Critics see it differently. Some First Nations leaders say it could undermine their constitutional rights. Unions argue it threatens the ability of workers in federally regulated industries to go on strike. Environmental groups have dubbed it the “Bulldoze Nature Bill”.

Still, the bill is racing through Parliament, and the Liberals appear to want it to become law before the end of the year. So what does this legislation actually do? Why is the government in such a hurry to pass it? And what changes once it does?
Althia Raj, a national columnist with the Toronto Star, has been following the bill since it was first tabled in September.
